newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch firmer, seeks direction.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch firmer, seeks direction.

text.p: Precious metal markets largely marked time on Thursday awaiting clear direction ahead of Friday's Comex option expiry and the likelihood that Russia will begin exporting platinum group metals (PGMs) soon, dealers said.
"I'm not viciously bearish (for gold). I think we have seen the lows and $347/$348 should hold. But even if it doesn't there is good support at $341," one dealer said.
The focus for palladium was confirmation from a senior Almaz official that Russian exports could begin later this month.
"It's all down to how the Russians manage this situation. If they try to get three months lost revenue at once, then that is a bit bearish," one PGM dealer said.
Prices generally edged higher by the 1500 GMT gold fixing despite low volume and New York opening quietly. There was no knee-jerk selling some dealers had feared for palladium.
Gold fixed at $352.90 per ounce up $1.45 from the morning and $1.50 from Wednesday. An hour earlier palladium had fixed at $152.00 compared with $150.50 earlier and $151,50 on Wednesday.
Earlier Europe and the Far East markets were generally lower as sentiment in gold edged towards bearish, although there was late short covering in Hong Kong.

But dealers said physical interest in gold was still high witnessed by above-usual premiums being commanded by "four nines" 400 ounces bars over 99.95 purity products. Small bars were also getting premiums.

"There is good physical offtake but there is a lot of paper gold about," one dealer said referring to the decline in gold's one-month lease rate which was indicated today at 1.14 percent compared with 1.36 pecent at the beginning of the month.
Silver was unchanged at $5.24/$5.26, a couple of cents above its opening and technically robust and cheap enough to attract speculators if any of the other prices flopped, dealers said.
"Silver is starting to look interesting," one dealer said.
"(palladium)is going to get whipped about a bit until the Russia situation is clearer," a dealer said.

Russia, the largest exporter of palladium, has not shipped metal this year due to internal administrative problems and has yet to finalise its 1997 supply contract with Japan, the world's biggest user of the metal.
Exports this month or next would almost certainly be on a spot basis into the dealer market and that could provoke aggressive selling of the metal, dealers said.
